samples.name: helios
samples.identification: Native XOR binder carrying NjRAT 0.7d Horror Edition and a second Themida-protected executable
evidence: Entry 0x401475 calls main shim 0x4013ff then binder 0x40108c. Decoder 0x401000 allocates output and XORs input bytes with key[index % 32], returning decoded bytes.

Binder descriptor table points to two encrypted PE images at VA 0x402032 (56320 bytes) and VA 0x40fc4b (3020288 bytes). Decrypted names are Payload.exe and HeliosRed v1.5.exe; both use getenv(Temp). fopen(wb), fwrite and fclose precede ShellExecuteA(open, filename).

Recovered first PE SHA256 8175726a32ba618659dc88a12339af77c7b286734bfa22eeb6e5b5dadd068d3e. DN entry j.A.main calls j.OK.ko. ko calls INS, starts RC receive thread and kl.WRK keylogger thread unconditionally.

Configuration: H=DarkAlotaibi-48808.portmap.host, P=48808, separator Y262SUCZ4UJJ, version <- NjRAT 0.7d Horror Edition ->. connect uses the configured host/port with TcpClient; RC receives a length-framed buffer, passes bytes to _Lambda__1 and Ind dispatches operator commands.

kl.WRK polls keys 0..255 with GetAsyncKeyState, appends window context and mapped characters to Logs, and periodically stores logs through STV. Ind exposes keylog/clipboard/screenshot/plugin execution and destructive commands; MBRSlayer.Start opens PhysicalDrive0 for write and writes a 512-byte embedded boot-sector image.

Anti_CH, USB_SP, Idr, IsF, Isu and BD are False; Defender-stop/UAC/task-scheduler switches are Disabled. These are implemented capabilities rather than asserted enabled startup effects. C2 and keylogger thread startup are not behind those switches.

Second recovered PE SHA256 f17ad6c04f341ab13b9d4564783f7f6498ea4fe33ee794eb240730c99a90bf70. Its entry 0x8b3058 begins an unpacking stage; .themida is RWX virtual storage, .boot contains protected startup. The protected application is unresolved; the independently recovered RAT is sufficient for the wrapper verdict.

detection_coverage.outer: Two suspicious observations across anti-static/payload and process/deploy; three notable mechanics/format observations added. No hostile label invented for an encrypted binder technique also usable by legitimate packagers.
detection_coverage.decoded_rat: Existing hostile multi-source collection, MBR destruction and two NjRAT identities all retained; polling keylog and anti-Defender findings retained.
detection_coverage.gap: The scanner does not automatically reconstruct these variable-key embedded PE members. YAML recognizes reconstruction/staging but cannot expose all decoded RAT behaviors in the original analysis tree. ML probability rose from 0.82026356 to 0.9849357 but calibrated lvl remains -1; standalone decoded RAT is 0.995/lvl25/conf92.

samples.name: signed
samples.identification: Sleipnir Windows performance tuner 3.23.0.0, PS2EXE wrapper
evidence: Managed entry ModuleNameSpace.MainApp.Main reads the Sleipnir.ps1 manifest resource (364937 bytes), adds it to a System.Management.Automation runspace and executes it. Wrapper credential/read-key APIs support interactive PowerShell host UI; their presence is not credential theft or covert logging.

Full resource is readable PowerShell/WPF application logic: registry/service/network performance tweaks, hardware/system metrics, game cleanup, local backups/history and benchmarking. WPF Add_Click handlers call Invoke-ModeRun/Invoke-ProfileRun; destructive tuning does not run as an unsolicited install action at startup.

Gaming/maximum profiles add Defender exclusions for existing game directories and named game processes, then cull configured background applications. The existing suspicious defender-exclusion-process finding accurately describes this dual-use behavior and is unchanged.

Maximum profile can disable hypervisor/CPU mitigations/memory integrity; UI descriptions and tweak risks expose those effects, while Invoke-TweakApply backs up prior state before applying and checking it. These capabilities fit the tool purpose; they are not proof of hostile deployment.

GPU install path uses configured vendor HTTPS URLs, downloads to local driver_installers, requires Get-AuthenticodeSignature status Valid plus expected vendor subject, creates a restore point and only then launches the installer. Vendor pages are opened by explicit button action. No covert C2, secret harvesting, exfiltration, or unrelated payload is present in the inspected script.

PE image SHA256 digest 198fc01289e38f1072d6daaa62cf53be32c8558d477ebbda5d56042270b722f2 matches the Authenticode digest. CN=Sleipnir Local Publisher is self-issued; osslsigncode verifies the timestamp and confirms matching image digests but rejects public certificate-chain trust because the publisher is self-signed. A second osslsigncode verification with only the extracted publisher certificate as an explicit local trust anchor succeeds, independently establishing signature integrity. This does not confer public trust or vendor identity.

Forager recovered NVIDIA/Intel vendor pages as HTML; no payload executes from those pages because the signature guard fails. AMD configured URL redirects to an AMD Download-Incomplete page; forager exhausted retries after remote HTTP/2 errors, so no AMD installer was recovered. Placeholder self-elevation raw URL is gated out by REPLACE-WITH and is not configured.

Collection provenance and AV detections are acknowledged. PS2EXE admin execution, security-setting reductions, process termination and Defender exclusions plausibly explain heuristic detections. Actual deployment authorization and publisher provenance are unavailable; no deployment circumstances were invented. BENIGN is a sighted-quarantine judgment.
samples.trait_changes: None; all 188 findings including the suspicious Defender exclusion are unchanged.

samples.name: keyv
evidence: The supplied tgz SHA256 equals the independently fetched registry.npmjs.org Keyv 4.2.2 tarball exactly: 0d62d377e6deeb09fbe372fa10bb46b9bae348131c9ca722b7b1e1f9b13e083d.

Archive has README, package.json, src/index.js and src/index.d.ts only. No install lifecycle hook or concealed native/script payload. Runtime source implements EventEmitter errors, namespaced Map/store CRUD, TTL expiration, iterators, JSON-buffer serialization, and optional Brotli compression.

Computed require is restricted to the local adapter mapping selected by caller options/URI scheme. Database references are adapter choices, not brute-force account candidates. Optional adapters are caller-installed and unversioned here; no claim is made about arbitrary downstream deployment.

Fetched and inspected json-buffer 3.0.1, compress-brotli 1.3.6 and currently resolved 1.3.14, @types/json-buffer 3.0.0, and the unusual development dependency this 1.1.0. Compression versions share the same runtime implementation: promisified zlib Brotli and JSON-buffer. json-buffer handles tagged Base64 values without evaluation; @types contains declarations; this resolves the project-root module for tests. No unexpected install/network/shell/credential behavior appeared in these runtime implementations.
README URLs and database code are documentation/examples; the manifest clean command is an explicit developer script, not an automatic install action.

The cited Aikido article links to its August 2026 report explicitly identifying compromised Keyv 6.0.0, with setup.mjs, Math_Symbol.js and a preinstall hook. None are present in this older registry-identical 4.2.2 artifact. Package-name/version association during collection is the supported explanation for this label, not evidence of payload behavior.

trait_changes.reason: A declared package name and a Redis adapter key/value literal do not establish that an arbitrary file implements the library. Names/descriptions/placement now describe the observed facts. Matchers, severity, platforms and effective file-type scopes are unchanged.
trait_changes.consumers: All three exact adapter-mapping suppressor references in embedded-dict.yaml were retargeted. No matcher or exclusion population was narrowed. Ancestor well-known/lib and runtime selectors were inspected; no newly triggered attack claim appears in any original archive member. The separate nonfiring legacy source-path observation is retained unchanged.
trait_changes.losses: No capability or attack detection lost. Two identity-feature IDs were replaced by metadata IDs, including propagation to the archive parent. ML probability shifted from 0.25058985 to 0.448883 while lvl remains -1.

controls.summary: 11 focused controls passed: changed key period and bytes/output names; invalid MZ and invalid PE signatures; zero XOR key; unrelated file-path and stream bindings; adapter mapping; spoof package name; retained credential dictionary; existing outside-batch name catalog and SPN-positive fixture. No new suspicious traits on benign original samples.
controls.limitations: No live malware execution; static paths establish capabilities, not successful C2 or raw-disk writes. The second Themida-protected embedded application remains unresolved.

material_detection_losses: None. Accurate matches are retained; two weak Keyv identity observations are relocated, not removed.
